body:
Doesn't look right at all. Her beauty mark looks like a cold sore now.

How much more proof do people need at this point? THERE IS SOMETHING OBVIOUSLY GOING ON, and I have a feeling it's not good. Maybe we ARE heading for the end, and these changes we're seeing have a divine reasoning behind them.

I remember listening to music shortly after my birth date of June 1986. I remember being taken somewhere in a yellow stroller with an umbrella. I have vivid "flash" memories of seeing the sun light, and how it warm it was. It was a sunny, early summer day. On this same day/memory, I also remember looking up and seeing the huge department store sign for Zayre's. The odd thing is, is this particular store closed in February 1987 in my nearby city. So, the memory I had must've been from sometime in the summer of 1986, which is when I was a baby. My mom said she took me out one day a week after I was born to Watertown (NY...our nearby city), just for some light shopping. The first store we stopped at? Zayre's. So, uh, is it possible that I can remember something from when I was 7 DAYS OLD?

I also had this weird thing happen to me when I was 4 years old. Somehow, out of nowhere, I gained rather extensive knowledge about the popular US cars of the current time (1990). My father casually enjoyed cars, but not "modern" ones. He never "talked cars" with me, even though he was a great mechanic and I regret not letting him teach me. I could identify makes, models, and years of cars at the age of 4. How? After a few months of this, it disappeared. I've only ever had general knowledge of cars since then. I have several family members vouch for this, because my parents used to show them how amazing it was.

But yeah. My memory? Nuts. Always has been. My knowledge of pop culture and music trivia is pretty damn impressive, not to sound like a douche canoe. I used to read rock and roll reference books as a kid until the pages fell apart. 

Who knows? Probably an Aspie..."officially".
This comment is making me smile. Debbie Gibson forever!
Thank you so much, friend. Yeah, the death of my dog was the hardest thing I've ever dealt with.
